topic: Using std::merge to Combine Sorted Ranges
explanation: In C++, the std::merge algorithm is used to efficiently combine two sorted ranges into a single sorted range. This function is essential when merging datasets while maintaining order, leveraging the properties of sorted sequences to perform the merge in linear time. It exemplifies the use of the Standard Template Library (STL) algorithms, iterator concepts, and modern C++ practices for generic programming.
syntax:
template <class InputIt1, class InputIt2, class OutputIt>
OutputIt merge(InputIt1 first1, InputIt1 last1, InputIt2 first2, InputIt2 last2, OutputIt d_first);
example_explanation: This example demonstrates merging two sorted vectors of integers into a single sorted vector using std::merge. It highlights how C++ STL algorithms operate on iterators, enabling efficient, generic, and modern data processing. The code maintains sorted order and showcases best practices such as reserving space beforehand and using range-based iteration for output, illustrating modern C++ idioms.
